claim_reviews.rationale: Lancaster pp. 707–709 describes Roman caementa hand laid in mortar and use of light volcanic rock for vaults; pp. 711–713 document Rome cases including scoria and tuff. Origin unknown avoids priority claim.
Lancaster p. 711 sample 021 states scoria, vault of a room facing the forum portico and date 46–44 BCE; date represents authors’ room context rather than a demonstrated invention date.

Lancaster pp. 712–713 reports a north aisle fragment, alternating material, building date AD 112; Bianchi p. 82 separately describes fragment 10, with aisle attribution qualified as probable. By-112 bound reflects the building dedication, not an independent sample date.

Lancaster pp. 713 and 724–725 identifies sample 05, frigidarium buttressing arches, building context 298–305 CE and trace-element match to Campi Flegrei. District inference is analytical, not a named quarry.

Earliest is explicitly limited to the sampled cases in this record; Lancaster pp. 707–709 distinguishes large caementa from fine mortar aggregate and pp. 711, 725 leave phasing and reasons for source change open.
Lancaster pp. 708–710 discusses historic dome petrography and the later study’s sample selection; no Pantheon quarry or carrier is established. This retains an explicit evidence question.

Lancaster p. 713 supports the Pantheon–Ulpia material comparison; Mark and Hutchinson pp. 26–30 model lower uncracked hoop stress in their density configurations, not a demonstrated transmission or the effect of scoria alone. Bianchi documents the Ulpia fragment, not a Pantheon relationship. Remove or defer the established edge and its supplied_method/contributing/high-confidence attributes unless independent informative evidence supports the causal process relation. A carefully scoped non-causal comparison and model result may be retained with attribution; do not infer a transfer.
